title: Largest Philippines crypto exchange, Coins.ph, said to face central bank regulatory action
summary: The exchange, which has over 18 million customers, is said to have handled business transactions involving restricted offshore gaming and gambling companies.
content: Coins.ph, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the Philippines with over 18 million customers, is reportedly facing regulatory action from the central bank. The exchange is said to have processed business transactions tied to restricted offshore gaming and gambling companies.
content_ta: பிலிப்பைன்ஸ் நாட்டின் மிகப்பெரிய cryptocurrency பரிமாற்ற நிறுவனமான Coins.ph, மத்திய வங்கியின் ஒழுங்குமுறை நடவடிக்கையை எதிர்கொள்ளக்கூடும் என்று கூறப்பட்டுள்ளது. 18 மில்லியனுக்கும் அதிகமான வாடிக்கையாளர்களைக் கொண்டுள்ள இந்த நிறுவனம், தடைசெய்யப்பட்ட ஆஃப்ஷோர் கேமிங் மற்றும் சூதாட்ட நிறுவனங்கள் தொடர்பான வணிகப் பரிவர்த்தனைகளைக் கையாண்டதாகக் கூறப்படுகிறது.

title: Deloitte survey: 52% of UK CFOs expect AI to cut headcount
summary:
AI's potential to reduce jobs without boosting profits may lead to jobless growth, pressuring policymakers to balance tech adoption with employment.
The post Deloitte survey: 52% of UK CFOs expect AI to cut headcount appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: A recent Deloitte survey reveals that 52% of UK CFOs anticipate artificial intelligence will reduce headcount within their organizations. This trend raises concerns regarding potential jobless growth, as firms prioritize technological efficiency over workforce expansion. These findings suggest that policymakers may face increasing pressure to address the broader economic implications of AI adoption, balancing the drive for innovation with the necessity of maintaining employment levels across the United Kingdom.
content_ta: Deloitte நடத்திய சமீபத்திய ஆய்வின்படி, 52% UK CFO-க்கள் செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு (AI) மூலம் தங்கள் நிறுவனங்களில் பணியாளர்களின் எண்ணிக்கை குறையும் என்று எதிர்பார்க்கின்றனர். நிறுவனங்கள் வேலைவாய்ப்பு உருவாக்கத்தை விட தொழில்நுட்ப செயல்திறனுக்கு முன்னுரிமை அளிப்பதால், இது வேலையில்லா வளர்ச்சிக் குறித்த கவலைகளை எழுப்பியுள்ளது. தொழில்நுட்ப வளர்ச்சியை ஊக்குவிப்பதற்கும், அதேசமயம் UK-வில் வேலைவாய்ப்பு நிலைகளைத் தக்கவைப்பதற்கும் இடையே சமநிலையை உருவாக்க வேண்டிய கட்டாயம் கொள்கை வகுப்பாளர்களுக்கு ஏற்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: US government Bitcoin holdings fall to 328,372 BTC in 2026
summary:
The US government's strategic Bitcoin reserve management may stabilize market concerns over potential large-scale liquidations, impacting crypto dynamics.
The post US government Bitcoin holdings fall to 328,372 BTC in 2026 appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: The United States government's Bitcoin holdings have decreased to 328,372 units in 2026. This shift in the government's strategic digital asset reserve management is being closely monitored by market observers. Analysts suggest that the current management approach may help stabilize market concerns regarding potential large-scale sell-offs, ultimately influencing broader cryptocurrency market dynamics. This update highlights the ongoing institutional impact of government-held Bitcoin on the industry.
content_ta: 2026-ஆம் ஆண்டில், United States அரசாங்கத்தின் வசம் உள்ள Bitcoin இருப்பு 328,372 ஆகக் குறைந்துள்ளது. அரசாங்கத்தின் இந்த டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து மேலாண்மை மாற்றத்தை சந்தை ஆய்வாளர்கள் கூர்ந்து கவனித்து வருகின்றனர். இத்தகைய மேலாண்மை நடவடிக்கைகள், சந்தையில் ஏற்படக்கூடிய பெரிய அளவிலான விற்பனை குறித்த அச்சத்தைக் குறைத்து, ஒட்டுமொத்த கிரிப்டோ சந்தையின் போக்கில் தாக்கத்தை ஏற்படுத்தும் என்று நிபுணர்கள் கருதுகின்றனர். அரசாங்கத்தின் இந்த Bitcoin இருப்பு மாற்றங்கள் சந்தையில் முக்கியமான தாக்கத்தை ஏற்படுத்துகின்றன.

title: Anthropic asks full appeals court to revisit Pentagon national security ruling
summary:
The case highlights tensions between national security concerns and constitutional rights, potentially impacting future AI industry regulations.
The post Anthropic asks full appeals court to revisit Pentagon national security ruling appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Anthropic has formally requested that a full appeals court re-examine a recent ruling involving the Pentagon and national security. The legal dispute underscores the ongoing tension between safeguarding sensitive government interests and the constitutional protections applicable to the AI industry. As AI companies continue to face increased regulatory scrutiny, the outcome of this case could establish important legal precedents for how technology firms engage with national security mandates.
content_ta: Anthropic நிறுவனம், Pentagon மற்றும் தேசிய பாதுகாப்பு தொடர்பான சமீபத்திய நீதிமன்றத் தீர்ப்பை முழு மேல்முறையீட்டு நீதிமன்றம் மீண்டும் மறுபரிசீலனை செய்ய வேண்டும் என்று கோரியுள்ளது. அரசின் தேசிய பாதுகாப்பு நலன்களுக்கும், AI நிறுவனங்களின் அரசியலமைப்பு உரிமைகளுக்கும் இடையே நிலவும் மோதலை இந்த வழக்கு எடுத்துக்காட்டுகிறது. AI நிறுவனங்கள் மீதான ஒழுங்குமுறை நடவடிக்கைகள் அதிகரித்து வரும் நிலையில், இந்த வழக்கின் முடிவு தொழில்நுட்ப நிறுவனங்கள் தேசிய பாதுகாப்பு விவகாரங்களை எதிர்கொள்ளும் முறையில் முக்கியமான முன்னுதாரணத்தை உருவாக்கலாம்.

title: Polymarket weighs an equity path against a token launch

content: Polymarket is reportedly considering a transition toward an equity-based model instead of pursuing a token launch. This strategic shift could significantly impact the platform's future market approach, investor relationships, and influence broader industry standards for decentralized prediction markets. The company is currently evaluating these potential paths to determine which direction best aligns with its long-term growth and regulatory considerations.
content_ta: Polymarket நிறுவனம் தனது எதிர்கால சந்தை வியூகத்தை மாற்றியமைக்கும் நோக்கில், டோக்கன் வெளியீட்டிற்குப் பதிலாக பங்கு அடிப்படையிலான (equity-based) மாதிரியைப் பின்பற்றுவது குறித்து பரிசீலித்து வருகிறது. இந்த முக்கிய மாற்றம் முதலீட்டாளர்களின் அணுகுமுறை மற்றும் இந்தத் துறையின் தரநிலைகளில் பெரிய தாக்கத்தை ஏற்படுத்தக்கூடும். தனது நீண்டகால வளர்ச்சி மற்றும் ஒழுங்குமுறை விதிகளை மனதில் கொண்டு, எந்தப் பாதையைத் தேர்ந்தெடுப்பது என்பது குறித்த ஆய்வில் Polymarket ஈடுபட்டுள்ளது.

The company will focus on power management systems and high-capacity equipment designed specifically for Nvidia-powered AI factories. These advancements aim to support the growing demands of large-scale artificial intelligence operations, highlighting Compal’s commitment to expanding its footprint in the AI hardware sector during this premier industry event.
content_ta: 2026 ஆம் ஆண்டிற்கான OCP Global Summit நிகழ்வில், Compal நிறுவனம் தனது அதிநவீன உள்கட்டமைப்பு தீர்வுகளை காட்சிப்படுத்தவுள்ளது. Nvidia தளங்களுக்காக பிரத்யேகமாக வடிவமைக்கப்பட்ட சக்தி மேலாண்மை அமைப்புகள் மற்றும் உயர் திறன் கொண்ட AI தொழிற்சாலை உபகரணங்களை நிறுவனம் முன்னிலைப்படுத்துகிறது. பெரிய அளவிலான செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு செயல்பாடுகளுக்கான வளர்ந்து வரும் தேவைகளை பூர்த்தி செய்வதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டு, இந்த முக்கிய தொழில்முறை நிகழ்வின் மூலம் AI வன்பொருள் துறையில் தனது இருப்பை Compal பலப்படுத்துகிறது.

title: Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore unveil on-device AI tool to fight chat scams
summary:
The collaboration could enhance user privacy and security, but its success hinges on timely updates and integration with popular apps.
The post Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore unveil on-device AI tool to fight chat scams appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore have announced a collaboration to develop an on-device artificial intelligence tool aimed at identifying and blocking chat-based scams. By processing data directly on the user's device, the technology seeks to bolster privacy and security without relying on cloud-based servers. The effectiveness of this protective tool will ultimately depend on its seamless integration into mobile applications and consistent updates against evolving fraudulent tactics.
content_ta: Google DeepMind மற்றும் GovTech Singapore ஆகியவை இணைந்து, சாட் மூலம் நடக்கும் மோசடிகளைக் கண்டறிந்து தடுக்கும் வகையிலான புதிய 'ஆன்-டிவைஸ்' செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு கருவியை உருவாக்கியுள்ளன. இந்தத் தொழில்நுட்பம் பயனர் தகவல்களை மேகக்கணிக்கு (cloud) அனுப்பாமல், சாதனத்திலேயே நேரடியாகச் செயல்படுத்துவதால் கூடுதல் பாதுகாப்பும் தனிமனித சுதந்திரமும் உறுதி செய்யப்படுகிறது. செயலிகளில் இந்தத் தொழில்நுட்பத்தை முறையாக ஒருங்கிணைப்பதும், புதிய மோசடி யுக்திகளுக்கு ஏற்பத் தொடர்ந்து புதுப்பிப்பதும் இதன் வெற்றியைத் தீர்மானிக்கும்.

title: Rubio to visit India next week to boost energy cooperation, investment
summary:
Rubio's India visit may shift energy dynamics, influencing U.S. political outcomes and economic conditions amid global market fluctuations.
The post Rubio to visit India next week to boost energy cooperation, investment appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Senator Marco Rubio is scheduled to visit India next week to strengthen energy cooperation and promote mutual investment. The visit comes as both nations aim to deepen economic ties and navigate complex global market dynamics. Observers suggest this diplomatic trip could play a significant role in shaping future U.S. political and economic strategies while potentially impacting the regional energy sector and international trade partnerships.
content_ta: Senator Marco Rubio அடுத்த வாரம் India-வுக்கு பயணம் மேற்கொண்டு, அங்கு எரிசக்தி ஒத்துழைப்பு மற்றும் முதலீடுகளை மேம்படுத்துவது குறித்து பேச்சுவார்த்தை நடத்த உள்ளார். இரு நாடுகளுக்கும் இடையிலான பொருளாதார உறவுகளை வலுப்படுத்துவதையும், உலகளாவிய சந்தை மாற்றங்களை கையாள்வதையும் நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டு இந்த பயணம் அமைகிறது. இந்த ராஜதந்திர பயணம் எதிர்கால U.S. அரசியல் மற்றும் பொருளாதார உத்திகளை வடிவமைப்பதில் முக்கிய பங்கு வகிக்கும் என்று எதிர்பார்க்கப்படுகிறது.

title: Coins.ph faces potential license loss over alleged offshore gambling links
summary:

content: Coins.ph is currently facing the potential loss of its operating license due to allegations involving offshore gambling connections. This regulatory scrutiny threatens to impact user trust within the exchange and may influence broader regional approaches to cryptocurrency oversight. As the situation develops, the stability of the platform remains a key concern for its user base and the digital asset industry.
content_ta: Offshore சூதாட்ட தளங்களுடன் தொடர்பு இருப்பதாக எழுந்த புகாரைத் தொடர்ந்து, Coins.ph தனது உரிமத்தை இழக்கும் அபாயத்தை எதிர்கொண்டுள்ளது. இந்த ஒழுங்குமுறை நடவடிக்கைகள், அந்த தளத்தின் மீதான பயனர்களின் நம்பிக்கையை பாதிப்பதுடன், பிராந்திய அளவில் கிரிப்டோகரன்சி தொடர்பான கட்டுப்பாட்டு முறைகளிலும் மாற்றத்தை ஏற்படுத்தலாம். இந்த விவகாரம் தற்போது கிரிப்டோ சந்தையில் பெரும் கவனத்தை ஈர்த்துள்ளது.

title: X Money Offers 3% Cash Back, Up to 6.00% APY
summary: X Money, the Fintech arm of social media platform X, is currently promoting its services, providing up to 3% cash back on purchases and up to 6%  APY on “balances in qualifying US states.” X Money is currently available in 41 U.S. states and Washington... Read More
content: X Money, the financial services division of the social media platform X, is promoting its banking features to users. The platform is currently available across 41 U.S. states and Washington D.C., as it continues to expand its reach within the United States market.
content_ta: சமூக ஊடக தளமான X-ன் நிதிச் சேவை பிரிவான X Money, தனது வங்கிச் சேவைகளை பயனர்களுக்கு ஊக்குவித்து வருகிறது. தகுதியுள்ள U.S. மாகாணங்களில் உள்ள வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கு, கொள்முதல் செய்யும் போது 3% வரை கேஷ் பேக் மற்றும் கணக்கு நிலுவைத் தொகைக்கு 6.00% வரை வட்டி (APY) வழங்கப்படுகிறது. தற்போது 41 U.S. மாகாணங்கள் மற்றும் வாஷிங்டன் டி.சி.-யில் இந்தச் சேவை கிடைக்கிறது.

title: Upgrade Applies for Nevada ILC Charter to Launch Its Own FDIC Insured Bank
summary: San Francisco-based fintech Upgrade has moved to secure its own banking platform by filing applications for a Nevada industrial loan company charter. The Fintech-focused company submitted the paperwork on October 12, 2026, to both the Nevada Financial Institutions Division and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, seeking... Read More
content: San Francisco-based Upgrade is seeking to establish its own banking platform. The company has officially filed applications for a Nevada industrial loan company charter with both the Nevada Financial Institutions Division and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation. This strategic move aims to enable the fintech firm to launch its own FDIC-insured bank, expanding its operational capabilities and regulatory status within the United States financial system.
content_ta: San Francisco-ஐ தளமாகக் கொண்ட Upgrade நிறுவனம் தனது சொந்த வங்கித் தளத்தை உருவாக்கும் முயற்சியில் ஈடுபட்டுள்ளது. இதற்காக, Nevada industrial loan company உரிமத்திற்கு, அந்த மாநிலத்தின் Financial Institutions Division மற்றும் Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ஆகிய அமைப்புகளிடம் நிறுவனம் விண்ணப்பித்துள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் FDIC காப்பீடு பெற்ற சொந்த வங்கியொன்றை உருவாக்கி, அமெரிக்க நிதிச் சந்தையில் தனது செயல்பாடுகளை விரிவுபடுத்த Upgrade திட்டமிட்டுள்ளது.

title: NFT Marketplace Blur Plans to Wind Down Web Interface Amid Drop in Trading Activity
summary: NFT marketplace Blur intends to retire the public-facing web interface at blur.io on November 12, 2026, while leaving its core on-chain marketplace protocol intact. The decision, disclosed in an official statement on X on October 12, reflects a prolonged collapse in trading activity across the... Read More
content: NFT marketplace Blur has announced plans to decommission its public web interface, blur.io, on November 12, 2026. The platform confirmed that while the website will be retired, the core on-chain marketplace protocol will remain fully operational. This strategic decision follows a period of significant decline in NFT trading activity, prompting the team to shift its focus away from the consumer-facing frontend while maintaining the underlying infrastructure for users.
content_ta: NFT marketplace Blur, தனது பொது இணையதள இடைமுகமான blur.io-வை நவம்பர் 12, 2026 அன்று முடக்கப்போவதாக அறிவித்துள்ளது. இணையதளம் மூடப்பட்டாலும், அதன் முக்கிய on-chain marketplace protocol தொடர்ந்து செயல்படும் என்று நிறுவனம் உறுதிப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. NFT வர்த்தக நடவடிக்கைகளில் ஏற்பட்டுள்ள தொடர்ச்சியான சரிவு காரணமாகவே, நுகர்வோர் எதிர்கொள்ளும் இந்த இடைமுகத்தை நிறுத்திவிட்டு, அடிப்படை உள்கட்டமைப்பை மட்டும் பராமரிக்க Blur முடிவு செய்துள்ளது.

title: Brickken’s Solving the Agentic Trust Problem
summary: Brickken co-founder and chief revenue officer Ludovico Rossi believes that, despite the attention given to agentic commerce, it won’t reach its potential until stakeholders are convinced there are enforceable controls over agents. They must also be assured that data can be reliably available on-chain and across systems.... Read More
content: Brickken co-founder and chief revenue officer Ludovico Rossi argues that the future of agentic commerce depends on building trust. To unlock its full potential, stakeholders need enforceable controls over autonomous agents. Additionally, ensuring that data remains reliably accessible on-chain and integrated across diverse systems is essential for wider adoption. These security and transparency measures are critical for Brickken as it navigates the emerging landscape of automated digital commerce.
content_ta: Brickken நிறுவனத்தின் இணை நிறுவனர் மற்றும் தலைமை வருவாய் அதிகாரி Ludovico Rossi, agentic commerce துறையில் நம்பிக்கையை உருவாக்குவதே அதன் வளர்ச்சிக்கு முக்கியம் என்று கூறுகிறார். தன்னாட்சி முகவர்கள் (autonomous agents) மீது வலுவான கட்டுப்பாடுகள் இருப்பது அவசியம். மேலும், தரவுகள் அனைத்தும் on-chain முறையில் பாதுகாப்பாகவும், பல்வேறு அமைப்புகளுடன் இணைந்தும் இருப்பதை உறுதி செய்வது, இந்தத் துறையின் வளர்ச்சிக்கு முக்கியமானதாக Brickken கருதுகிறது.

title: Statement on the Commission’s Approval of a Proposed Rule Change to Permit the Listing of Binary Options Overlying Key Performance Indicators
content: The Commission has officially approved a proposed rule change to permit the listing and trading of binary options based on key performance indicators. This regulatory update expands the range of financial instruments available for listing, establishing a framework for these specific types of options. The move aims to modernize market offerings while ensuring proper oversight of these instruments within the regulated financial exchange environment.
content_ta: Key Performance Indicators-ஐ அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்ட பைனரி ஆப்ஷன்களைப் பட்டியலிடவும் வர்த்தகம் செய்யவும் அனுமதிக்கும் விதிகளில் மாற்றத்தை மேற்கொள்வதற்கு கமிஷன் ஒப்புதல் அளித்துள்ளது. இந்த ஒழுங்குமுறை மாற்றமானது, நிதிச் சந்தையில் பட்டியலிடக்கூடிய கருவிகளின் வரம்பை விரிவுபடுத்துகிறது. ஒழுங்குபடுத்தப்பட்ட நிதிப் பரிமாற்றச் சூழலில், இத்தகைய புதிய வர்த்தகக் கருவிகளை முறையாகக் கண்காணிப்பதற்கும் நவீனப்படுத்துவதற்கும் இந்த நடவடிக்கை வழிவகுக்கும்.

title: Coinbase lays out flexible designs as key priority for Bitcoin’s post-quantum migration
summary: Coinbase published priorities for Bitcoin's post-quantum transition, urging early preparation for signature upgrades and fund migration.
content: Coinbase has outlined flexible designs as a key priority for Bitcoin's eventual post-quantum migration. The cryptocurrency exchange published its strategic priorities to address future quantum computing threats. Industry experts are urged to begin early preparations for necessary signature upgrades and secure fund migration strategies to protect the network from upcoming technological advancements.
content_ta: Bitcoin-ன் எதிர்கால post-quantum migration-க்கான முக்கிய முன்னுரிமையாக நெகிழ்வான வடிவமைப்புகளை Coinbase வெளியிட்டுள்ளது. எதிர்கால quantum computing அச்சுறுத்தல்களை எதிர்கொள்வதற்கான மூலோபாய முன்னுரிமைகளை இந்த cryptocurrency exchange வெளியிட்டுள்ளது. வரவிருக்கும் தொழில்நுட்ப முன்னேற்றங்களிலிருந்து network-ஐ பாதுகாக்க, தேவையான signature upgrades மற்றும் fund migration உத்திகளுக்காக முன்கூட்டியே தயாராகுமாறு தொழில் துறை வல்லுநர்கள் வலியுறுத்தப்படுகிறார்கள்.

title: NEAR falls 12% after $2.64M whale liquidation – Will $4.50 hold or break?
summary: It is either NEAR's correction has overstayed or its rally is close to an end.
content: The cryptocurrency NEAR recently experienced a significant 12% price decline following a $2.64 million whale liquidation. This drop has sparked intense debate among investors regarding the asset's future stability. Analysts are now closely monitoring whether the $4.50 price level will act as a strong support or if the current downtrend will continue, signaling that the previous rally might be nearing its end.
content_ta: NEAR கிரிப்டோகரன்சியின் விலை, $2.64 மில்லியன் மதிப்புள்ள 'வேல்' விற்பனைக்குப் பிறகு 12% சரிவைச் சந்தித்துள்ளது. இந்த வீழ்ச்சி, முதலீட்டாளர்கள் மத்தியில் கவலையை ஏற்படுத்தியுள்ளது. $4.50 என்ற விலை நிலை ஆதரவாக நீடிக்குமா அல்லது சரிவு தொடருமா என்பது தற்போதைய முக்கிய கேள்வியாக உள்ளது. NEAR-ன் இந்த விலை மாற்றம், அதன் முந்தைய முன்னேற்றம் முடிவுக்கு வருவதற்கான அறிகுறியா என்பதை சந்தை ஆய்வாளர்கள் கூர்ந்து கவனித்து வருகின்றனர்.

title: OpenAI in talks to acquire cybersecurity firm Trail of Bits
summary:
The potential acquisition could bolster OpenAI's financial stability and strategic positioning, reducing perceived bankruptcy risks.

content: OpenAI is reportedly in discussions to acquire the cybersecurity firm Trail of Bits. summary: The switch will replace Solana’s existing validator voting system, remove vote transactions from blocks and could sharply change headline transaction counts even if user activity stays flat.
content: Solana has scheduled the Alpenglow upgrade for October 21, aiming to achieve a 150-millisecond transaction finality. The upcoming switch will replace the network's existing validator voting system and remove vote transactions directly from blocks. These changes could significantly impact headline transaction counts, even if overall user activity on the blockchain remains unchanged.

content: Starknet has launched a new privacy feature called Shadow Accounts to enhance user anonymity within decentralized finance. content: New York Fed President John Williams has indicated that supply constraints driven by advancements in artificial intelligence could persist for over two years. title: Cross River Announces Evan L. Russo as President
summary:
CRB Group, Inc., the parent company of Cross River Bank, a leading technology infrastructure platform powering embedded financial solutions serving as the trust anchor for global banking and money movement, today announced that Evan L. Russo has been appointed President, effective October 1, 2026.  
Mr. Russo previously served as CEO of Lazard Asset Management and CFO of Lazard Ltd. and has served as Cross River’s Lead Independent Director since April 2026. Mr. Russo will report to Cross River Founder, CEO and Chairman, Gilles Gade, and will continue on the Board of Directors while relinquishing his role as Lead Independent Director. Shimshon Gross, who has served on the Board since Cross River’s inception in 2008, has been appointed Lead Independent Director. 
In his new role, Mr. Russo will partner with CEO Gilles Gade to accelerate Cross River’s growth, strengthen the company’s institutional operating model and further establish Cross River as the trusted infrastructure layer powering payments, banking, digital assets and AI-enabled financial services. He will help lead Cross River's global expansion while building the operational, financial and governance capabilities required to scale the company and support its next phase of growth. 
"Technology is revolutionizing how money moves around the globe, but it still moves through regulated infrastructure, which requires leaders who have built and led significant global financial institutions,” said Gilles Gade, Founder, CEO and Chairman of Cross River. “As we enter this next chapter, Evan and I will bring complementary strengths to the path ahead. I will continue to focus on our vision for the future of financial infrastructure, our technology, and strategic partnerships, while Evan brings the institutional leadership, strategic focus and operating discipline required to scale that vision. Together, we are building the leadership structure and capabilities to capture the significant opportunity ahead for Cross River.”  
Mr. Russo brings more than two decades of experience across investment banking, capital markets, asset management and financial services. Before joining Cross River’s Board, he served as CEO of Lazard Asset Management, where he led the firm’s global asset-management business. Previously, he served as CFO of Lazard Ltd. and Lazard Group and as co-head of Lazard’s Capital Markets and Capital Structure Advisory practice. As a Managing Director in Financial Advisory, he advised corporate clients on strategic M&A, restructuring and financial transactions.  
Before joining Lazard, Mr. Russo held positions in the Investment Banking Divisions of Goldman Sachs and Barclays Capital. He began his career as a corporate attorney at Milbank, Tweed, Hadley & McCloy. Mr. Russo received an MBA from The Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania, a JD from Columbia Law School, and a BA from Queens College. 
“Cross River has built something unique: a technology-driven financial infrastructure platform built on a regulated banking foundation, with the connectivity and capabilities to support the next generation of financial solutions,” said Evan L. Russo, President of Cross River. “As financial activity becomes increasingly programmable, global and AI-enabled, the importance of trusted, scalable and regulated infrastructure will only increase. Cross River is exceptionally well-positioned at the intersection of these powerful trends. I am excited to work alongside Gilles and the entire Cross River team to scale the platform, strengthen our institutional capabilities and position Cross River as the partner of choice for companies shaping the future of financial services.”

title: NatWest Improves AI Speech Recognition for UK Banking Customers with NVIDIA Nemotron
summary:
NatWest and NVIDIA have worked together to develop speech AI designed to better understand how the bank’s customers across the UK speak - from different accents and pronunciations, to the words, phrases and everyday language they use when talking about their money.
 
The collaboration combined NVIDIA's cutting-edge AI speech recognition technology with NatWest's leading AI research and its understanding of the millions of customers it serves across the UK. Together, researchers and engineers from both organisations set out to address a challenge facing the next generation of conversational banking services: improving how speech AI understands the wide range of accents, words, phrases and financial language used across the UK.
 
The work underpins NatWest's recently announced Spending Insights tool - a conversational AI service developed by the bank that allows customers to explore their finances using natural voice and text conversations – and showed the system to mishear 20% fewer words, with an overall reduction in Word Error Rate, the standard measure of speech-recognition accuracy, across the accents tested.
 
Spending Insights, which is now available to 75% of Royal Bank of Scotland customers as part of an ongoing rollout, allows customers to talk naturally about their finances using voice and text, asking questions about their spending, exploring trends and receiving personalised insights. Customers can interrupt, ask follow-up questions and provide additional context, with the experience combining conversational responses with interactive charts and visualisations.
 

Maja Pantic, Chief AI Research Officer, NatWest Group said,
“NatWest has built trusted relationships with customers across every nation and region of the UK, and we know they are increasingly using AI in their everyday lives. By understanding how their expectations are changing, we are using AI to strengthen our relationships and better support customer needs.
“That means customers being able to interact with us in a way that feels natural to them. If they choose to speak to AI, the technology needs to understand the different accents, words and everyday language used across the UK.
“We are continually learning and improving how we use AI to make banking simpler, more personal and more responsive, while maintaining the trust customers place in us. Working closely with NVIDIA has been an important part of helping us advance that work.”
Aser Blanco, Global Head of Banking from NVIDIA said: “Speech recognition becomes much more challenging when it has to work in real time and understand the accents, terminology and ways of speaking people use in everyday conversations. Working with NatWest has allowed us to apply NVIDIA Nemotron open-source models to those real-world banking challenges and identify where the technology can be improved. The results show how adapting speech applications to real-world language can make voice experiences more accurate and natural.”
 
NatWest selected NVIDIA Nemotron automatic speech recognition (ASR), which converts spoken words into text, for the speech-recognition element of Spending Insights. The resulting text is then interpreted by NatWest’s proprietary Small Language Models, helping the experience understand what a customer is asking and generate a relevant response.
 
The speech AI project began with in-depth testing with 90 NatWest colleagues from different parts of the UK, whose natural accents included Glaswegian, Northern Irish, Welsh, Yorkshire, Mancunian, Midlands, Southern English, non-British accents and more. Together, they recorded around 3,000 realistic banking questions.
 
Colleagues were asked not only to read scripted questions aloud, but also to ask them in their own words, using the phrases, pronunciations and more informal or colloquial language they would naturally use when talking about their finances.
 
Using these insights, NatWest researchers worked closely with NVIDIA specialists to identify where speech-recognition models performed well and where they found particular accents, pronunciations, words or ways of phrasing a question more difficult to understand.
 
The research also highlighted how seemingly small transcription errors can change the meaning of a banking question. For example, during testing, a Scottish colleague saying "last quarter" became "last water".
 
Researchers found that merchant names, dates and financial terminology could be particularly challenging for speech-recognition technology, despite being critical to understanding a customer's request correctly.
 
NatWest then expanded the work using anonymised contact-centre transcripts, allowing the model to learn from a much broader range of real-world banking language. This helped further improve how the model understands merchant names, financial terminology and the different ways customers describe their finances in everyday conversation.
 
The transcripts were anonymised and remained within NatWest’s secure environment. No NatWest customer data was shared with NVIDIA, and any adaptations made using NatWest data are ringfenced to the bank.
 
NatWest and NVIDIA will continue working together to optimise the speech-recognition technology as conversational banking experiences evolve, helping ensure customers can interact with services in the most natural and intuitive way possible.

title: Worldline Helps Establish First Global ISO 20125 Standard for Sustainable Digital Services
summary:
Worldline, a European leader in payment services, today adopts ISO/IEC 20125-1:2026, the world's first international standard for the eco-design of digital services. The standard gives enterprises a practical framework to measure, reduce and manage the environmental impact of their digital operations while supporting broader ESG and net-zero strategies.
Organisations increasingly face pressure from customers, investors, regulators and procurement teams to demonstrate environmental progress. Until now, they have lacked a consistent, internationally recognised methodology for improving the sustainability of digital services and proving measurable results to stakeholders. ISO/IEC 20125-1:2026 changes that.
Worldline led the two-year international collaboration to develop this standard, which defines 32 eco-design practices to help organisations improve digital services efficiency and embrace digital sufficiency: building and maintaining only what is needed, prioritizing value, reducing resource use and considering a service’s entire lifecycle.
Sébastien Mandron, CSR Director at Worldline, said: "For the first time, enterprises have an internationally recognised framework that aligns digital transformation with sustainability objectives. The standard turns digital responsibility from a strategic aspiration into operational reality.” 
The benefits extend beyond environmental impact. The standard provides a credible framework for responding to growing customer sustainability requirements, improving procurement credentials and demonstrating measurable ESG progress. By establishing a common language for environmental performance, it enables organisations that build digital services and those that procure them to evaluate sustainability using shared, verifiable criteria.
Vincent Courboulay, co-founder and Head of the INR Academy at the Institut du Numérique Responsable, which was one of the contributing organisations to the development of the standard added: "This standard creates a shared understanding between service providers and their customers. It transforms responsible digital principles into concrete, measurable commitments that both sides can track and verify.”
ISO/IEC 20125-1:2026 is now available from ISO and national standards bodies worldwide. title: SBS Launches Banking’s First Sovereign AI Platform
summary:
SBS, the global financial technology company that more than 1,500 financial institutions rely on to digitally transform the way they operate, launched the first sovereign AI platform purpose-built for generative and agentic AI in core banking. The SBS AI Foundation, powered by NVIDIA, lets banks deploy AI without data ever leaving their own environment, whether on a private cloud, a managed cloud or fully on-premises. The platform is already live in production with a long-time SBS client in the UK, Scottish Building Society, on Amazon Web Services and is now available to hundreds of financial institutions SBS serves across the world.
Banks are under real pressure to use AI to speed up decisions, reduce operational costs and compete with digital-first challengers. But most financial institutions operate under strict regulations, from GDPR to country-specific data residency requirements, that limit how customer and transaction data can be processed. As a result, banks can’t route sensitive data through external AI providers, which is how most enterprise AI platforms were built to work. According to Gartner, while 84% of finance organizations have implemented or are planning to implement AI, only 7% report high or very high impact from those investments. The gap between AI ambition and results is largely due to the fact that, until now, there has been no infrastructure to run generative and agentic AI at scale within a bank’s own walls.
The platform runs on NVIDIA infrastructure, with NIM microservices powering the AI layer and NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails keeping every response within the bank's regulatory boundaries. It pulls together data from across a bank's entire SBS infrastructure, from core banking and lending to digital banking and regulatory reporting, and makes it immediately available to generative AI and autonomous agents. In production with Scottish Building Society, the solution is already delivering approximately 30-40% faster response times with more consistent outputs, while maintaining the full explainability and audit trail that regulators require.
SBS AI Foundation streamlines operations across three areas for banks:
Generative AI grounded in each institution’s own data. AI-guided customer onboarding and engagement that uses a bank’s own records and product portfolio to surface the right product for the right customer at the right moment, accelerating time-to-value, operational efficiency, product design and personalisation all with powerful Explainable AI (XAI).
Natural language intelligence for faster decisions. A generative AI co-pilot that translates complex data queries (on structured and unstructured data) into insights, replacing multi-day reporting cycles and giving product teams and executives the intelligence they need at their fingertips, to move from insight to action without waiting on analyst queues.
Sovereign risk intelligence with a full regulatory audit trail. AI-powered risk monitoring that surfaces risk and compliance exposure, and generates a complete audit trail, all without sending risk data outside the institution’s controlled environment.
In the near future, the solution will encompass Agentic AI, which automates core banking workflows with autonomous agents that execute multi-step banking processes, transparently with human oversight and within a fully governed environment.
“Banks want AI they can trust, explain and run wherever their data must live. By building with NVIDIA, we can give our customers that assurance without compromising on governance,” said Eric Bierry, CEO of SBS. “We are already seeing the results from this work with our early customers, and we look forward to continuing to roll out these capabilities as we help more financial institutions take advantage of AI efficiencies.”
The platform marks the first deployment of NVIDIA's full AI stack, including NIM, NeMo Guardrails and open Nemotron models, within a live core banking system, across markets where data residency rules are strictest, including under GDPR in Europe and across data-resident markets in Africa.
“SBS is turning a governed AI runtime into a shared intelligence layer beneath its entire banking platform,” said Aser Blanco, Global Head of Banking at NVIDIA. “With NVIDIA, SBS is giving banks the tools they need to deploy generative and agentic AI across cloud and sovereign infrastructure. Once they have this infrastructure in place, the capabilities it unlocks drive efficiency and ultimately power growth.”

title: Sumsub Selects IPinfo to Bring Evidence-Backed IP Intelligence to Fraud Prevention
summary:
Sumsub, a trust infrastructure platform serving over 4,000 clients across financial services, crypto, trading, and iGaming, has selected IPinfo as its primary source of IP geolocation and VPN detection. IPinfo's data is embedded directly into Sumsub’s platform, supporting KYC and fraud prevention checks for customers who may have to defend their decisions to auditors and regulators.
For fintech and verification companies, IP intelligence is moving beyond a background enrichment signal to become part of the infrastructure behind critical decisions. Sumsub's adoption of IPinfo demonstrates that as these platforms adapt to growing complexity, they are looking beyond basic IP signals toward data that is not only accurate, but measurable, explainable, and supported by evidence.
When customers questioned why individual IP addresses had been flagged as risky, Sumsub needed clear evidence to support their classifications. That level of transparency wasn’t readily available, and Sumsub needed IP intelligence it could confidently stand up to scrutiny.
"Our customers rely on the signals we provide to make decisions they may ultimately have to defend to their auditors,” said Sumsub’s co-founder and CTO Vyacheslav Zholudev. “So we have to be able to substantiate every signal we pass on. That is the standard we hold our data providers to. That data informs decisions long after onboarding, so it has to hold up every time. Accuracy is easy to claim and hard to prove." 
Measuring against Sumsub's known traffic, IPinfo delivers the higher country-level accuracy and fewer of the large location errors that matter most in fraud and compliance decisions. IPinfo correctly identified the country for 98.77% of the IP addresses tested, placed half of all results within 20 km of the corresponding GPS position, and put fewer than 6% more than 500 km away.
As IP intelligence becomes more deeply embedded in verification platforms, the expectations placed on the underlying data are becoming more rigorous.
“When verification platforms build third-party data into their products, the quality of that data directly affects their reputations,” said IPinfo Founder & Co-CEO Ben Dowling. “Providing the evidence behind our data has always been foundational to IPinfo, from how we measure the internet to how we investigate and substantiate an individual result when it’s challenged.”
Beyond geolocation, IPinfo provides data on location precision, anonymization and hosting infrastructure, and the network behind an IP address. Together, these signals give Sumsub a more complete view of an IP address, adding context its customers can use to make and defend decisions at every stage, from onboarding to continuous monitoring.

title: Christmas ‘Moneymaxxing’: Consumers Turn to Flexible Payment Options Ahead of the Festive Season
summary:
UK consumers are ‘moneymaxxing’ this Christmas as they look for ways to plan ahead and make their festive budgets work harder by spreading the cost of purchases over multiple months.
New research, commissioned by payments network Affirm and carried out by Savvy Marketing, reveals that almost half (47%) of those planning to start their Christmas shopping earlier are doing so to spread the cost of items across several paydays.
More than a third (35%) of consumers expect to spread their Christmas spending over two months and 27% across three. For retailers, this suggests meeting consumers’ demands for payment flexibility could be key to winning during the extended festive shopping period.
Catherine Shuttleworth, retail expert and CEO at Savvy, said: “Consumers are becoming more deliberate about how they plan their Christmas spending. The rise of ‘moneymaxxing’ reflects an increasing number of shoppers turning to flexible payments this holiday season, with many starting earlier and spreading festive spending across more paydays than in the past. For retailers this means being ready to trade Christmas well from the start of the Golden Quarter is increasingly important. They also need to adapt to how people now want to shop and pay, offering frictionless payment options at the checkout to give shoppers more flexibility to manage their Christmas spending over time.”
Flexible payment options are becoming an important part of how consumers plan and manage Christmas spending, with almost half (44%) of consumers saying they are likely to use Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) for Christmas shopping, increasing to 57% among under-45s.
Of these consumers, half (50%) plan to use BNPL to spread payments across several paydays, while a fifth (21%) say it will allow them to buy a higher-quality gift.
New BNPL regulations introduced this summer could also influence Christmas spending decisions. More than a third (35%) of shoppers say knowing about the new regulation has made them more likely to consider using BNPL, rising to 47% among under-45s.
Ruth Spratt, UK Country Manager at Affirm, said: “Consumers are much more deliberate about how they spend at Christmas, planning purchases earlier, thinking carefully about what they buy and choosing payment options that work for them. The best payment options support that mindset by making the total cost clear upfront, setting out exactly when payments are due and avoiding late or hidden fees. For retailers, the opportunity is to give shoppers transparent choices that help them plan ahead and spend with confidence.”
Affirm enables customers to spread the cost of their purchases over time, with no late fees or hidden charges.

title: Vivid Selects Wise Platform for International Payments for SMEs

The partnership comes as Vivid sees rapidly growing demand for international payments among its business customers. Over the ten months to May 2026, the number of Vivid Business customers making an international payment in a given month grew more than fivefold1.
Growth has been particularly strong in major trading hubs outside Europe, including China, the UAE and Singapore. Through its partnership with Wise Platform, Vivid Business customers will be able to make fast, transparent international payments into more than 40 currencies. CNY payouts are already available across 27 European countries and the next currencies are to be rolled out soon. 
Alexander Emeshev, Co-Founder at Vivid, said: "The modern entrepreneur is cosmopolitan, so their business banking should be. Cross-border payments are therefore essential for today's business banking. The growth we've seen over the past six months in customers sending money to markets like China, the UAE, and Singapore is proof of that demand. Together with Wise, we're now meeting that demand: offering the same speed and transparency when moving money to Shenzhen as when moving it to Stockholm."
Manuel Sandhofer, General Manager for EMEA at Wise Platform, said: “As European SMEs do more business around the world, their payments need to keep pace with their ambitions and work just as well across borders as they do at home. That means the same speed, transparency and reliability wherever they’re moving money. We’re excited to work with Vivid to bring the infrastructure Wise has built to make that possible for more businesses across Europe.”
Wise Platform is powered by Wise’s global payments network, more than 80 licenses and direct access to domestic payment systems in nine markets worldwide, enabling 77% of its payments to arrive instantly, in under 20 seconds. Vivid joins a growing number of leading institutions including Monzo, UniCredit, Raiffeisen Bank International and N26 using Wise Platform to deliver a seamless and reliable experience that meets the evolving expectations of their customers.
Vivid payment services are provided by Vivid Money S.A., an Electronic Money Institution licensed by the CSSF in Luxembourg.

title: PEX Launches AI Built to Earn Finance Teams' Trust, One Workflow at a Time
summary:
PEX, a leading corporate card and spend management platform, today launched PEX AI, a set of capabilities that automates everyday finance work, runs multi-step workflows and connects PEX to AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. Built around a crawl, walk, run approach, PEX AI gives teams a way to hand off more work as trust grows while staying in control.
PEX's 2026 State of Finance Report, a survey of 687 finance and operations leaders, found that more than half are interested in each AI capability tested, yet just 31% use AI in finance. Trust is the top barrier: 36% name trust in AI accuracy as the biggest obstacle to using more of it.
“The businesses that keep our economy moving deserve the same advances in AI as the world's largest enterprises,” said Toffer Grant, founder and CEO of PEX. “We're making those capabilities practical and accessible for the finance teams managing day-to-day operations, starting with work that saves time. When AI touches financial decisions, trust has to be earned.”
Crawl: Automate everyday finance work
Nearly a third of finance teams lose more than 20 hours a month to manual receipts, coding and reconciliation. PEX AI starts there:
AI receipt and invoice matching: PEX reads each receipt and matches it to transactions, so finance stops chasing Cardholders.
AI-powered GL coding: PEX suggests the right GL code from the team's history.
Bill reading: PEX reads and extracts details from bills, reducing manual data entry.
PEX Agent: admins ask about transactions, balances or their account in plain language and get the answer.
Walk: Turn insights into action
Once the basics run on their own, PEX AI takes on work with more steps and more at stake:
Multi-step automation: one request sets up 20 card groups, cards or spend rules, in place of 50 clicks.
Action from the chat: admins act on what the PEX Agent finds, such as out-of-policy spend, without leaving the conversation.
Anomaly detection (coming soon): PEX AI flags unusual spending activity for finance teams to review.
AI audit history: PEX logs and explains account changes, so admins know what changed and why.
Run: Put routine workflows on autopilot
At this stage, AI works wherever finance teams work. The PEX MCP server, now in beta, connects PEX to AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot Studio. Account administrators can find transactions missing receipts, review spend or check balances by asking in the AI tools they already use.
“Every stage of PEX AI has to earn the next,” said Alex Najem, CTO of PEX. “First AI proves it can handle a task. Then it takes on a workflow. Then it runs the routine and flags what needs a person. Finance stays in control of what AI can do and can see the work at every step.”

title: Standard Chartered Appoints Ying Ying Tan as Global Head of Securities Services
summary:
Standard Chartered today announced the appointment of Ying Ying Tan as Global Head of Securities Services, effective immediately. In her role, she will lead the Bank’s Securities Services business globally, responsible for driving the strategy, growth and continued development of the franchise across custody, fund services, clearing and related securities infrastructure solutions.
Ying Ying succeeds Margaret Harwood-Jones who has taken on the role of CEO, UK & Europe at Standard Chartered.
In addition to her Securities Services role, Ying Ying has also been appointed as Global Head of Digital Assets, effective immediately. In this role, she will be responsible for driving the execution of the Bank’s digital assets agenda working across businesses and functions to scale the development and building of the Bank’s capabilities across custody, tokenisation, digital asset trading, financing and broader ecosystem partnerships. She will continue to report to Ole Matthiessen, Global Head, Transaction Services & Digital Assets, and be based in in Singapore.
In her digital asset role, Ying Ying will work closely with René Michau who has taken on a senior advisory role also reporting to Ole Matthiessen. René who has been instrumental in building and shaping the Bank’s digital assets franchise, will remain closely involved in its next phase of growth. He will continue to support the Bank’s digital assets franchise and contribute his deep expertise as a key member of the Group’s Digital Assets Steering Committee.
The appointment reflects the increasing convergence of traditional and digital finance as clients seek seamless access to a broader range of assets, market infrastructures and investment opportunities. Over the past few years, Standard Chartered has established digital assets capabilities spanning custody, tokenised deposits, trading and tokenised money market funds. The Bank continues to invest in the infrastructure, partnerships and expertise required to support clients as the market evolves.
Ole Matthiessen, Global Head of Transaction Services & Digital Assets, Standard Chartered, said: “Ying Ying brings a unique combination of expertise across securities services, transaction banking and digital assets. She has played a pivotal role in building and commercialising our digital assets custody capabilities while developing the breadth of our Securities Services franchise to meet our clients’ evolving needs. Her appointment reflects the strength of our talent pipeline; her leadership, experience and track record of execution position her exceptionally well to lead the next phase of growth as we continue to strengthen our Securities Services franchise and advance our digital assets agenda.”
Since joining Standard Chartered in 2017, Ying Ying has held a number of senior leadership roles and most recently served as Global Head of Securities Services Product Management and Chief Operating Officer for the business. She has played a key role in building and commercialising the Bank’s digital assets custody business and advancing its securities services broader product management strategy, helping position Standard Chartered at the forefront of the convergence between traditional and digital financial markets.
Prior to joining Standard Chartered, Ying Ying Tan held several regional and global leadership positions at Deutsche Bank across securities services, product management and transaction banking.
Ying Ying Tan, Global Head of Securities Services and Global Head of Digital Assets, Standard Chartered, said: “The boundaries between traditional and digital finance are becoming increasingly interconnected, creating new opportunities for clients and the industry. Standard Chartered continues to build and invest in our capabilities supported by our international network, market expertise and commitment to innovation. I look forward to working with our clients, partners and teams around the world to help shape the next phase of growth of our Securities Services business and our ambitious digital assets agenda.”
Standard Chartered has been at the forefront of driving innovation in securities services and in digital assets with a focus on building institutional grade capabilities while providing the trust, safety and international connectivity needed to support long-term institutional growth. The Bank has built capabilities across custody, tokenisation, trading, financing and market infrastructure, while working closely with clients, regulators, market infrastructures and industry partners to help shape the future of the ecosystem.
